items.headline: TSMC posts $46.7B Q3 revenue, says AI demand still exceeds supply, and guides Q4 to $52.3-54.3B
items.why: The foundry that makes most leading AI chips reports demand above capacity and a 2026 capex budget of $60-64B, which is the strongest hard-data counterweight to this week's AI-funding fears.

sources.title: TSMC third quarter revenue tops guidance as CEO says AI demand still exceeds supply

items.headline: Chip and AI-infrastructure stocks sell off on AI-funding worries: Lam Research about -9%, CoreWeave about -10% on Thursday
items.why: The market is now pricing the cost of capital behind AI buildouts rather than the demand, so any financing stress at the leveraged end of the chain hits the whole semiconductor complex.

items.headline: Memory and AI-cloud names slide midweek after hot inflation print: Micron -5.6%, SK Hynix -6.6%, CoreWeave more than -16%
items.why: Memory has been the biggest driver of 2026 chip revenue, so a rate-driven de-rating there compounds the broader AI sell-off.

sources.title: Nvidia stock sinks as chip sell-off deepens on hot inflation data

items.headline: Meta falls about 7% after earnings and a 2-for-1 split; Tesla slips about 3% despite an earnings beat
items.why: Even beats and corporate actions were sold, with investors focused on spending plans (Tesla's lower 2026 capex but higher 2027-28 outlay), which shows the market is punishing capital intensity.

items.headline: US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about $228M of net outflows and Ether ETFs about $320M in the week of Oct 12-16
items.why: Both major products lost money in the same week, so the institutional bid that supported prices earlier in the year is not currently there.

items.headline: Median top-500 token fell about 5.8% over the weekend, the steepest weekend drop since April; Ether trades near $2,420
items.why: Altcoins are falling harder than Bitcoin, which is the usual signature of risk being pulled out of the long tail first.

items.headline: Bitcoin slips back below $82,000 as the equity sell-off spreads on Thursday
items.why: Bitcoin is trading with tech and rate expectations rather than as a hedge, so equity and yield moves are the near-term driver.

items.headline: September US CPI runs at 3.7% headline and 2.6% core year on year, driven by fuel costs
items.why: Inflation above 3.5% with energy as the driver keeps the Fed on a tightening path and pressures long-duration assets.

items.headline: Markets still price three more Fed and ECB hikes while Hormuz and Ukraine risks lift energy prices
items.why: Central banks face energy-led inflation with no clear demand slack, so the policy path stays hawkish unless oil retreats.

items.headline: US 10-year yield falls below 5% (4.95%) for the first time since Sept 23, down from a 5.36% high on Oct 7
items.why: Haven buying in the equity rout pulled yields back from the highs, which matters because long-end yields have been the main pressure on valuations.

items.headline: Record US interest expense and Chinese Treasury holdings at an 18-year low weigh on long-end yields
items.why: Fiscal supply and weaker foreign demand add a term-premium floor under yields regardless of the Fed.

items.headline: Brent reaches $111.75, a five-month high; WTI near $100 on renewed Gulf strikes
items.why: Oil at these levels feeds directly into the inflation prints and rate-hike pricing that are hitting equities and gold.

sources.title: Stock market today: S&P 500, Nasdaq tanks as tech stocks sink amid AI trade worries

items.headline: Tanker strikes near Hormuz cut shipments to 11.6M barrels per day in the week to Oct 13, versus a 17.15M baseline
items.why: A one-third loss of flow is a physical supply shock rather than a risk premium, which is why crude gained nearly 8% last week.

items.headline: Gold settles at $4,060.40, its lowest in more than two months
items.why: Higher oil and rate-hike odds are outweighing safe-haven demand, so gold is trading as a real-yield asset right now.

items.headline: Silver posts a fourth straight weekly decline, down more than 6% last week; copper futures near $6.60 per pound
items.why: Silver is falling on yields and the dollar while copper is held up by Chilean supply disruption, so the two metals are being driven by different forces.

items.headline: S&P 500 closes at 7,663 (-1.2%) and Nasdaq Composite at 26,008 (-2.6%); Dow flat at 52,866
items.why: The split between a flat Dow and a sharply lower Nasdaq shows the damage is concentrated in tech and chips rather than broad.

items.headline: Semiconductor index (SOX) closes at 10,690, just above its 200-day average at 10,677, which it has not breached since June 2025
items.why: That average is the line that separates a pullback within an uptrend from a trend break; SOX is already more than 26% off its June 22 record close.

items.headline: VIX peaks at 20.30 on Thursday, below the 22.31 high of Oct 16
items.why: Volatility is elevated but has not made a new high, so the sell-off is not yet accelerating.

items.headline: Bitcoin falls below $82,000 and is testing the $81,700-82,000 support zone flagged on Oct 19; next levels were $81,000 then $80,000
items.why: If that zone gives way, the next tests are $81,000 and the round-number $80,000 area.
